evidence: src/application/advance-order-use-case.ts: `if (!isOrderStatus(targetStatus)) { throw new DomainError("VALIDATION", "Unknown order status"); }` writes the status-validation rule inline.
src/application/list-orders-use-case.ts: `assertOrderStatus(status);` uses the domain's shared guard for the same rule.

src/application/get-stock-levels-use-case.ts: maps products to StockLevelDto inline (`productId: product.id, ... reserved: product.reservedQuantity`) instead of using a mapper the way order use cases use toOrderDto.
src/application/order-dto.ts: declares `StockLevelDto` next to the order DTOs, although it belongs to the stock concern.
src/application/advance-order-use-case.ts and src/application/cancel-order-use-case.ts: both contain `throw new DomainError("NOT_FOUND", `Order ${orderId} not found`)`.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Overall the module holds together: it is a set of order and stock use cases that share OrderDto and toOrderDto. One problem fails the rubric. The rule for rejecting an invalid order status is enforced in two different ways. ListOrdersUseCase uses the domain's assertOrderStatus. AdvanceOrderUseCase does not use it. Instead it calls isOrderStatus and throws its own DomainError("VALIDATION", "Unknown order status"). The error code and message are therefore defined in the use case as well as in the domain guard, so the two can drift apart. This counts as both duplicating a rule and bypassing the shared abstraction.

There are also two smaller inconsistencies that I am not reporting as violations:
- GetStockLevelsUseCase builds StockLevelDto inline instead of using a mapper, unlike the order use cases, which all use toOrderDto.
- StockLevelDto is declared in order-dto.ts even though it has nothing to do with orders.
The "Order ${orderId} not found" lookup appears in both AdvanceOrderUseCase and CancelOrderUseCase. This is minor, routine guard code.

violations.message: AdvanceOrderUseCase writes its own status check (isOrderStatus plus throw new DomainError("VALIDATION", "Unknown order status")) instead of using the domain's assertOrderStatus guard, which ListOrdersUseCase uses. This bypasses the shared guard and duplicates the rule, with its error code and message, outside the domain.
